t: Baekje founded its capital in the area in 18 BCE, Silla took the region in 553, and Goryeo built a southern capital there before the Joseon dynasty made Hanyang its planned capital in 1394.
Under Japanese rule from 1910 the city was renamed Gyeongseong and lost its status as a capital; it took the name Seoul after 1945, and four battles for it in the Korean War left it mostly in ruins.
After the war the city was rebuilt and in 1963 more than doubled in size, taking in Gangnam; its population peaked at over 10 million and has since decreased.
dyk: In the Korean War Seoul changed hands four times between June 1950 and the spring of 1951, and one estimate puts the damage at no fewer than 191,000 buildings, 55,000 houses and 1,000 factories in ruins.
ev: Baekje founds its capital, Wiryeseong, in the area of present-day Seoul
Silla takes control of the region from Baekje
Yi Seong-gye chooses Hanyang as the capital of the Joseon dynasty
Gojong proclaims the Korean Empire and the city is temporarily called Hwangseong
Japan annexes Korea and renames the city Gyeongseong
The charter of the City of Seoul names the city Seoul and makes it a municipal corporation
The Korean War begins and Seoul changes hands four times
Two annexations more than double the size of the city

f.founded: Baekje founded its capital, Wiryeseong, in 18 BCE, believed to lie within the bounds of present-day Seoul; Yi Seong-gye, founder of the Joseon dynasty, chose Hanyang as his new capital in September 1394, and construction began in October 1394.
f.where: On both banks of the Han River in the north-west of South Korea, in a mountainous and hilly landscape with Bukhansan on its northern edge.
f.known: Wiryeseong, the capital of Baekje; the Joseon capital of Hanyang and Hanseong; the Fortress Wall and its gates; the Five Grand Palaces; Japanese rule as Keijo; the four battles for the city in the Korean War; the rebuilding of the city and the growth of Gangnam
f.today: Seoul is the capital and largest city of South Korea, with about 9.6 million residents, and the only special metropolitan city in the country.
